units.summary: Test now builds a two-step breaker to match the new groupBreaker type. Assertions are unchanged, so a line-by-line review can be skipped.
units.headline: Reconcile test uses two-step circuit breaker
units.reason: Test-only type swap to match the production breaker type; no assertions removed or changed.

units.summary: Test now builds the old breaker as a two-step breaker to match the new groupBreaker type. Assertions are unchanged, so a line-by-line review can be skipped.
units.headline: Changed-key reconcile test uses two-step breaker
units.reason: Test-only type swap to match the production breaker type; no assertions removed or changed.

units.summary: handlerEntry now holds a groupBreaker (two-step) and a per-handler watches context with its cancel func. Reconcile ends that context when the handler is replaced or removed, so watches on it terminate.
units.headline: handlerEntry gains two-step breaker and per-handler watch context
units.reason: Struct field changes and a new cancellation lifecycle that decides when in-flight watches are terminated.
focus: Entries built directly in tests or elsewhere without watches/endWatches (nil context) are handled by serveWatch
Every replacement or removal path cancels the old entry's context exactly once

units.summary: New constructor creates a handler entry with a fresh closed breaker and a cancelable watch context. It replaces the inline struct literal and in-place mutation in reconcile.
units.headline: New constructor gives each handler its own cancelable watch context
units.reason: Creates a context per entry whose cancellation ends client watches; a leak or missed cancel changes runtime behavior.
focus: Each created entry's endWatches is eventually called, or the context leaks
Fresh breaker per entry matches the prior reset-on-change semantics

units.summary: The published serving entry now carries the groupBreaker type and the handler's watches context, so request-time code can bind a watch to its backend's lifetime.
units.headline: servingEntry carries watch context and two-step breaker
units.reason: Struct field added and retyped; it feeds the request path that decides when watches end.
focus: Other constructors of servingEntry set watches or tolerate nil
Snapshot readers see a watches context consistent with the handler they serve

units.summary: The router now creates a router-wide watches context at construction. It is cancelled by closeWatches at service stop so streaming watches end and shutdown does not wait on them.
units.headline: Router creates a router-wide watch context at construction
units.reason: Introduces the shutdown cancellation scope for long-lived watches.
focus: Watches started after closeWatches has run end immediately rather than hanging shutdown
Routers constructed in tests or other callers still get a live context

units.summary: Changed groups are now replaced with a new handlerEntry rather than mutated in place. Replaced and removed entries are collected and their watch contexts cancelled after publish, so clients re-watch against the new backend.
units.headline: Reconcile replaces changed entries and ends their watches after publish
units.reason: Changes the replace/remove semantics and terminates in-flight client watches on backend change.
focus: Order: publish before endWatches so a re-watching client sees the new entry
Anything holding the old *handlerEntry pointer after the replacement instead of mutation
Early-return and error paths in reconcile that skip cancelling retired entries

units.summary: The published servingEntry now includes the handler's watches context, so HandleFunc can scope a watch to its backend.
units.headline: publish copies watch context into serving snapshot
units.reason: Propagates the cancellation context that controls watch lifetime into the request path.
focus: Entries with a nil watches context (test-built handlerEntry) don't crash serveWatch
